title: The Environment Interface: reset and step
learning_objectives: Implement reset() and step() with the Gymnasium return signature
Distinguish terminated (the task ended) from truncated (a time limit hit)
Make stochastic environments reproducible with a seed passed to reset
Run an episode loop with any policy function
entry_point: class LineWorld(n=5, start=0, slip=0.0, max_steps=20); run_episode(env, policy, seed=None)
hints: Keep `self.done` and `self.steps`; set them in `reset` and check `self.done` at the start of `step`.
`move = 1 if action == 1 else -1`; if `self.slip > 0 and self.rng.random() < self.slip`, flip it; then `max(0, min(self.n - 1, self.state + move))`.
`terminated = self.state == self.n - 1`; `truncated = not terminated and self.steps >= self.max_steps`; `self.done = terminated or truncated`.

failure_feedback.advice: Reward 1.0 and terminated=True exactly when the new state is n - 1.
Clip moves at the walls; truncate when steps reach max_steps; refuse to step after the end.
Check the constructor arguments and the action value.
Re-seed in `reset(seed)` and draw one `rng.random()` per step only when slip > 0.
Reset the state, the step counter and the done flag.
